question: Poor environmental sanitation in a community is most directly linked to outbreaks of which disease?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Osteoporosis
options.D: Hypertension

explanation: Cholera is a waterborne disease spread easily when sanitation and safe drinking water systems fail. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the main goal of giving a standard clinical vaccine?

options.A: To provide immediate chemical relief from chronic joint inflammation
options.B: To destroy all existing white blood cells in the patient's body
options.C: To permanently block the liver from metabolizing oral medications
options.D: To introduce safe antigens that stimulate long-term memory cells

explanation: Vaccines give a harmless 'practice preview' of an infection so the immune system can build memory cells and protect the patient later. [learn more](GST114_U4_T2#GST114_U4_T2_h8)

question: A nurse manager sees a report saying patient wait times have a very large standard deviation. What does this mean for the clinic?

options.A: The clinic has successfully eliminated all delays in patient care
options.B: The average wait time is dangerously high for every single patient
options.C: Every patient is waiting the exact same amount of time to be seen
options.D: Wait times vary widely, with some patients waiting a very short time and others waiting extremely long

explanation: You nailed it! A large standard deviation means big differences—some patients are seen immediately while others wait forever, showing the clinic's service is quite inconsistent. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T2#GNS217_U4_T2_h7)

question: During a head-to-toe check, you notice something unusual in the abdomen. What's your next move?

options.A: Ignore the finding until the patient goes home
options.B: Perform a more focused, in-depth regional assessment of the abdomen
options.C: Document it as normal variation without further check
options.D: Skip the rest of the exam and immediately discharge the patient

explanation: When you spot an abnormality, zoom in! Do a closer, focused check on that specific body area to gather all the clinical details you need. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h6)

question: What happens to perishable foods when transport infrastructure is poor?

options.A: They last much longer without refrigeration.
options.B: They spoil before reaching the market.
options.C: They become much cheaper to buy for villagers.
options.D: They turn into dry grains automatically.

explanation: Without good roads and cold storage transport, fresh foods easily rot before they can make the long journey to market. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T022#GNS227_U2_T022_h7)

question: Why should you as a nurse care about what your patient likes or is used to eating?

options.A: Hospital management requires a daily report on tribal food choices
options.B: It helps the nurse order the exact same meal for every ward bed
options.C: Dietary habits directly impact wound healing and recovery speed
options.D: Patients refuse medications if their food preferences are ignored

explanation: Spot on! When patients enjoy their food and it fits their background, they eat better, heal faster, and avoid poor nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h1)

question: Which hormone from the pituitary gland triggers ovulation right in the middle of the cycle?

options.A: Luteinizing hormone
options.B: Thyroid-stimulating hormone
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Think 'LH surge!' A sudden spike in Luteinizing Hormone (LH) is the exact trigger that causes the ovary to release the egg. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h4)

question: A healthy toddler suddenly starts eating less food than before. What is the most likely reason for this?

options.A: Growth velocity naturally slows down after infancy, reducing food demand
options.B: The child is entering a severe phase of permanent nutritional failure
options.C: Breast milk or formula is no longer needed in any form
options.D: The child has developed an irreversible eating disorder

explanation: Don't panic if a toddler's appetite dips! Because growth slows down after year one, they simply don't need as many calories per kilogram. It's completely normal. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h3)

question: Which medication is routinely given right after baby is born to prevent heavy bleeding?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Paracetamol
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin is our best friend in the third stage of labor! It makes the uterus clamp down tight, squeezing off blood vessels to keep bleeding under control. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h7)

question: Which statement describes a study with good external validity?

options.A: The measurement tool produced the exact same score on repeated testing
options.B: The researchers strictly controlled all extraneous variables in the lab
options.C: The sample size was large enough to calculate a valid percentage
options.D: The results can be safely generalized to patients in other healthcare settings

explanation: Think of external validity as your study's passport—it means the findings can travel out of the lab and apply to real patients elsewhere. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T4#GNS224_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why must a National Drug Policy tie in closely with the National Health Policy?

options.A: It allows pharmaceutical companies to set their own market prices without government interference.
options.B: International donors will refuse to release funds if the two policies are separate documents.
options.C: Medications are essential therapeutic tools required to achieve overall population health goals.
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to purchase hospital supplies out of their own pockets.

explanation: You can't achieve a healthy nation without medicines! Because drugs are our most common tool for treatment, the drug policy has to support the country's bigger health goals. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T1#GNS215_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is a low blood albumin level usually a sign of long-standing (chronic) liver trouble rather than a sudden issue?

options.A: Albumin is stored in large amounts in fat tissue before being released
options.B: Acute liver injury causes albumin to temporarily hide inside the kidneys
options.C: Albumin has a long half-life, so levels drop slowly over weeks of poor production
options.D: The body stops producing red blood cells before it stops making albumin

explanation: You're getting the hang of this! Because albumin stays in circulation for about three weeks, it takes a while of poor liver production for levels to noticeably crash. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T11#GNS221_U2_T11_h3)

question: Why is it so urgent to use an AED immediately during a sudden cardiac arrest?

options.A: Emergency services cannot track patients without active AED pads
options.B: It replaces the need to ever perform chest compressions
options.C: It permanently cures any underlying chronic heart diseases
options.D: Survival chances drop quickly for every minute without a shock

explanation: Every single minute counts! The chance of survival goes down by about 10% for every minute a shock is delayed. Fast action saves lives. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is the main function of the LGA PHC Development Committee?

options.A: Manufacturing vaccines for the entire country
options.B: Treating emergency trauma cases at teaching hospitals
options.C: Designing the national university medical curriculum
options.D: Allocating resources and coordinating health services across the entire local government

explanation: The LGA committee oversees all primary health care activities within its local government area, ensuring fair distribution of resources and personnel. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h4)

question: A client with schizophrenia is stable and ready for discharge from a tertiary psychiatric hospital. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Keep the client admitted for another year to prevent any possibility of relapse
options.B: Advise the client to stop taking medications since their mood is now normal
options.C: Prepare a discharge summary and link the client to their local primary health clinic
options.D: Send the client home without informing local clinic staff

explanation: Great nursing care means bridging the gap! Writing a good summary and linking the patient to their local clinic ensures they won't default on their meds. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why are shellfish like shrimp and crabs not allowed in a traditional kosher diet?

options.A: They are classified as land animals
options.B: They are harvested during forbidden months
options.C: They consume blood from other marine life
options.D: They lack fins and scales

explanation: According to kosher rules, acceptable seafood must have both fins and scales, which rules out bottom-feeding shellfish like crabs and shrimp. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T019#GNS227_U2_T019_h4)

question: What do we call it when a doctor's expert advice strongly convinces a patient to use more medical services than they might have otherwise?

options.A: Supplier-induced demand
options.B: Third-party payment inflation
options.C: Market equilibrium pricing
options.D: An immunization externality

explanation: Exactly! Because patients trust doctors blindly, the experts can sometimes drive up the demand for their own treatments. [learn more](GST322_U1_T2#GST322_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of milieu therapy on a psychiatric ward?

options.A: Creating a safe and therapeutic environment for recovery
options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital building maintenance
options.C: Isolating disruptive patients from the general public
options.D: Testing new experimental pharmaceutical products

explanation: Milieu therapy uses the physical layout and daily social interactions on the ward to create a secure, structured space where healing can happen. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T2#GNS314_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is the main reason for preparing a wet mount during a pelvic exam?

options.A: To measure the exact daily urine output of the patient
options.B: To identify specific microorganisms like yeast or parasites under a microscope
options.C: To drain excess fluid from swollen labial glands
options.D: To check if the patient is pregnant

explanation: A wet mount lets the clinician quickly mix a discharge sample with a drop of fluid and peek under a microscope to spot the tiny culprits (like yeast or trichomonas) causing the trouble. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT standard personal protective equipment (PPE) for a field rescuer?

options.A: High-visibility vest
options.B: Sterile surgical gown
options.C: Hard hat
options.D: Steel-toed boots

explanation: You nailed it. Surgical gowns belong in the operating theatre, not out in the mud and rubble where hard hats and boots keep you safe! [learn more](GNS315_U5_T3#GNS315_U5_T3_h5)

question: If you eat more carbohydrates than your body needs right away, how is the extra sugar stored?

options.A: As free fatty acids floating in the spinal fluid
options.B: As liquid calcium deposits in the bone marrow
options.C: As glycogen in the liver and skeletal muscles
options.D: As raw amino acids inside the red blood cells

explanation: When there is extra sugar floating around, your liver and muscles quickly pack it together into a storage form called glycogen for later use. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T8#GNS121_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why should nurses never use ordinary kitchen spoons to measure out liquid medicines?

options.A: Liquid medications will stain metal spoons permanently
options.B: Hospital policy strictly forbids touching any utensil from a kitchen
options.C: Plastic spoons react chemically with syrup and destroy the drug
options.D: Household spoons vary widely in size and do not provide accurate doses

explanation: Spot on! Kitchen spoons come in all shapes and sizes, which can easily lead to giving too much or too little medicine. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T6#GNS125_U2_T6_h5)

question: In the microbiology lab, what is the main job of PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)?

options.A: Measuring physical cell length under oil immersion
options.B: Staining cell walls purple or pink
options.C: Amplifying specific segments of microbial DNA
options.D: Determining patient immune response levels

explanation: PCR is like a microscopic photocopier—it takes a tiny piece of germ DNA and makes millions of copies so scientists can easily spot it. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h6)

question: When is the right time to start the secondary survey?

options.A: Only after the patient is discharged home
options.B: While the patient is actively in cardiac arrest
options.C: Before checking if the patient has a clear airway
options.D: After the primary survey is done and the patient is stable

explanation: Always make sure immediate life threats in the primary survey are handled before moving on to a detailed secondary survey. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T2#GNS315_U3_T2_h4)

question: How do non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) mainly work in the body?

options.A: By putting the central nervous system to sleep
options.B: By releasing natural endorphins in the spine
options.C: By attaching straight to brain opioid receptors
options.D: By blocking prostaglandins at the injury site

explanation: NSAIDs like ibuprofen stop the body from making prostaglandins—the chemical helpers that cause swelling and pain right where you got hurt. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T2#GNS123_U3_T2_h5)

question: In Nigeria, what traditional support system has historically cared for most older adults?

options.A: International charity organizations
options.B: The extended family system
options.C: Government-run nursing homes
options.D: Private health insurance agencies

explanation: You've got it! Culturally, our extended family network in Nigeria takes the lead in housing and looking after our aging relatives. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T4#GNS321_U3_T4_h7)

question: How would you explain 'psychological resilience' in everyday clinical practice?

options.A: The ability to completely avoid all stressful events in life
options.B: A permanent immunity to developing any form of anxiety or sadness
options.C: The capacity to recover and adapt when facing major life hardships
options.D: A physical condition where the brain ignores emotional pain entirely

explanation: Spot on! Resilience isn't about dodging stress—it's about bending without breaking and bouncing back when life knocks you down. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T2#GNS314_U6_T2_h6)

question: What ethical principle supports a patient's right to make their own choices about their care plan?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Negligence
options.C: Maleficence
options.D: Paternalism

explanation: Autonomy is all about self-determination—respecting the patient's right to understand their options and make decisions about their own body and treatment. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T2#GNS314_U1_T2_h8)

question: Why is maintaining patient confidentiality particularly difficult during community health nursing practice?

options.A: Community nurses are legally required to publish patient records online
options.B: Patients prefer sharing their medical diagnoses with all their neighbors
options.C: Hospital rules forbid nurses from keeping health records locked away
options.D: Home visits and close-knit neighborhoods make privacy harder to protect

explanation: In small communities and during home visits, neighbors often notice health workers visiting, which makes keeping medical information private challenging. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h8)

question: How can a nurse show cultural humility when facing traditional family hierarchies?

options.A: Ignore the patient entirely and speak only to the community leader
options.B: Respect local traditions while still creating a safe space for individual patient input
options.C: Insist that patients completely abandon their cultural beliefs upon entering the hospital
options.D: Follow the hierarchical demands without ever asking the patient their opinion

explanation: Spot on! Cultural humility means respecting culture while making sure the individual patient still has a strong voice in their care. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T6#GNS312_U4_T6_h6)

question: A nurse makes a drug dosage mistake and now gets very nervous and avoids preparing intravenous medications. What is this behavior called?

options.A: Aggressive confrontation of peers
options.B: Intentional insubordination to management
options.C: Professional indifference and apathy
options.D: Hypervigilance and avoidance behavior

explanation: It's natural to want to run away from tasks that remind us of a painful mistake. Identifying this avoidance helps us address the fear rather than just hiding from it. [learn more](GST319_U6_T4#GST319_U6_T4_h2)

question: Why are reflex actions so much faster than normal, everyday movements?

options.A: They travel directly through the heart to save distance.
options.B: They use electrical impulses instead of chemical neurotransmitters.
options.C: They completely bypass initial processing in the brain.
options.D: They rely on faster motor fibers than sensory fibers.

explanation: Spot on! Because reflexes don't wait for the brain to think things through, the signal takes a quick shortcut straight through the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T25#GNS211_U3_T25_h1)

question: After fats are broken down in the small intestine, where do they go first?

options.A: Blood capillaries directly
options.B: The large intestine wall
options.C: Lymphatic lacteals
options.D: The gastric mucosa

explanation: Unlike sugars and amino acids that jump straight into blood capillaries, digested fats take a special detour through tiny lymphatic vessels called lacteals first! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T011#GNS227_U1_T011_h5)

question: Who typically leads a peer-led HIV support group?

options.A: A licensed medical doctor or surgeon
options.B: A hospital laboratory technician
options.C: A veteran community member living with HIV
options.D: A government health policy maker

explanation: Peer-led groups are guided by individuals who share the lived experience of managing the condition successfully. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h2)

question: A public hospital lacks funds to buy a new CT scanner and partners with a private firm to supply and run it. What is the key benefit here?

options.A: Complete removal of government oversight from radiological services
options.B: Guaranteed free healthcare services for every citizen in the region
options.C: Lower wage requirements for nurses operating the new machinery
options.D: Immediate access to advanced technology without massive upfront government spending

explanation: By partnering up, the hospital gets the equipment patients need right now without waiting years for public funds to clear. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why is lactic acid so important during food fermentation?

options.A: It acts as a natural preservative by lowering pH
options.B: It adds a sweet flavor to the food item
options.C: It turns the food liquid before consumption
options.D: It speeds up the rate of food spoilage

explanation: Great job thinking about this! Lactic acid makes the environment too acidic for bad bacteria to survive, which naturally preserves the food. [learn more](GST114_U3_T5#GST114_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the main danger of disconnecting the catheter tubing from the drainage bag?

options.A: It breaks the closed system and lets bacteria enter
options.B: It triggers severe allergic reactions to the plastic
options.C: It causes immediate permanent damage to the urethral sphincter
options.D: It creates high pressure that bursts the balloon

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the drainage system sealed and closed is the single best way to protect your patient from getting a catheter-associated infection. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T20#GNS212_U1_T20_h7)

question: A ward always has rushed handovers because staff arrive late. What is the best way to fix this?

options.A: Allow outgoing nurses to leave before the incoming shift arrives
options.B: Cancel all shift handovers permanently and rely on text messages
options.C: Reduce the amount of patient care required during the day
options.D: Implement strict arrival policies and use a structured handover checklist

explanation: Using a checklist alongside clear punctuality rules keeps handovers organized, quick, and right on track! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h8)

question: What makes a 'cytokine storm' so dangerous in severe COVID-19 patients?

options.A: It causes widespread tissue damage and multi-organ failure
options.B: It permanently blocks the absorption of oral medications
options.C: It causes a sudden and permanent drop in blood pressure only
options.D: It immediately destroys all white blood cells in the body

explanation: Spot on! A cytokine storm is like an immune system overdrive. It floods the body with inflammatory signals that end up harming healthy organs. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS123_U4_T6#GNS123_U4_T6_h1)

question: How should pain medication be given for chronic cancer pain according to standard guidelines?

options.A: Only when the pain becomes unbearable
options.B: Only when the patient remembers to ask
options.C: On a regular schedule around the clock
options.D: Strictly as a single bedtime dose

explanation: Scheduled dosing keeps the pain under control smoothly, rather than waiting for it to spike and trying to chase it down. Smart nursing care! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h7)

question: What does the term asepsis mean?

options.A: The presence of helpful bacteria on the skin
options.B: The absence of disease-producing microorganisms
options.C: The complete destruction of all body cells
options.D: The growth of pathogens in a wound

explanation: Asepsis literally translates to a- (without) sepsis (poison or infection), meaning the absence of harmful germs. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why shouldn't patients chew or swallow sublingual or buccal medications right away?

options.A: The medication will instantly crystallize in the stomach
options.B: Swallowing destroys the first-pass effect protection and digestive enzymes may break down the drug
options.C: Swallowing increases the absorption speed too much
options.D: Chewing causes severe irritation to the inner cheek lining

explanation: If they swallow it like a regular pill, stomach acid and the liver (first-pass metabolism) will chew it up and weaken the drug before it even gets to work. Let it dissolve where it is! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T15#GNS125_U3_T15_h2)

question: Why do nurses give routine immunizations to patients?

options.A: To stimulate adaptive immunity and build long-term memory cells
options.B: To instantly kill any bacteria currently residing in the bloodstream
options.C: To trigger an immediate innate response via localized vasodilation
options.D: To replace missing white blood cells in immunosuppressed clients

explanation: You're doing great! Vaccines give a safe preview of a germ so your adaptive system can build memory cells for future protection. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h8)

question: Who must be involved to make a school health programme truly successful?

options.A: External security contractors and police officers
options.B: Only the school principal and government auditors
options.C: Teachers, parents, and local healthcare workers
options.D: Strictly the senior students in the graduating class

explanation: School health is a collaborative effort involving everyone who has a stake in the child's well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h8)

question: Why do many patients delay seeking medical help for faecal incontinence?

options.A: Doctors rarely ask about bowel habits
options.B: Feelings of shame and social stigma
options.C: The condition always resolves on its own
options.D: Lack of any physical discomfort

explanation: Social embarrassment and stigma often cause individuals to hide their symptoms, preventing them from receiving timely medical evaluation and support. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h1)

question: What does the term 'plethora' mean in a patient with polycythaemia?

options.A: Severe swelling in the lower legs
options.B: A ruddy, reddish skin complexion
options.C: Yellow discoloration of the eyes
options.D: A sudden drop in blood pressure

explanation: Plethora just describes that classic red or flushed face look because there are so many blood cells packed near the skin surface. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T8#GNS311_U2_T8_h4)

question: What can happen if you use a sensitive smart bed alarm on a patient who is fully independent and active?

options.A: Immediate mechanical failure of the bed's lifting actuators
options.B: Unnecessary anxiety for the patient and alarm fatigue for nurses
options.C: Automatic cancellation of physician medication orders
options.D: Rapid depletion of the bed's internal backup battery

explanation: If a bed keeps beeping every time an active patient moves, it stresses the patient out and trains staff to ignore the noise—which is called alarm fatigue! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h3)

question: What does the term NEAT stand for in nutrition and metabolism discussions?

options.A: New Estimated Adaptation Threshold
options.B: Normal Energy Absorption Technique
options.C: Nutritional Evaluation and Assessment Tool
options.D: Non-Exercise Activity Thermogenesis

explanation: NEAT is all about those extra calories you burn through daily movements that aren't formal gym workouts—like walking to class, cleaning, or even fidgeting! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T9#GNS121_U1_T9_h4)

question: Which patients should receive standard precautions in the hospital?

options.A: Patients admitted to surgical wards only
options.B: Only patients with confirmed viral infections
options.C: Every patient in the healthcare facility
options.D: Individuals with active pulmonary tuberculosis

explanation: Exactly! Standard precautions are universal. Treat every patient as if their body fluids could carry infection, keeping both them and yourself protected. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h2)

question: What do we call a person who carries a disease-causing germ without showing any signs of illness?

options.A: A host
options.B: A vector
options.C: A fomite
options.D: A carrier

explanation: Carriers look and feel healthy, making them dangerous because they can spread infections without anyone realizing it. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h2)

question: Which action is critical for breaking the chain of transmission during an infectious disease outbreak?

options.A: Waiting patiently for the disease to run its course naturally
options.B: Focusing solely on hospital administrative paperwork
options.C: Isolating infectious individuals and tracing their contacts
options.D: Stopping all routine cleaning supplies distribution

explanation: Great job! Finding who was exposed and keeping sick people away from healthy people is how you successfully halt an infection's spread. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h6)

question: As a nurse leader in a public hospital, what does public accountability mainly mean for you?

options.A: Ensuring doctors follow instructions given by senior nurse managers
options.B: Answering for actions, resource use, and care quality in public facilities
options.C: Raising private funds to run hospital wards without government help
options.D: Fulfilling personal career goals within a healthcare organization

explanation: Spot on! Public accountability simply means you take responsibility for how public funds, hospital supplies, and patient care are handled on your watch. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h1)

question: What is the main goal of vocational rehabilitation in mental health CBR?

options.A: To replace traditional school education for young children
options.B: To keep clients busy so they do not talk to their family members
options.C: To help clients learn practical skills for earning income and gaining independence
options.D: To train clients to become fully licensed medical doctors and nurses

explanation: Vocational training equips individuals with trades like farming or tailoring, enabling them to earn money and feel productive in society. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h5)

question: What does 'institutionalism' mean in mental health care?

options.A: The strict enforcement of hospital visiting hours for family members
options.B: The process of building new psychiatric hospitals in rural areas
options.C: The loss of independent living skills from long hospital stays
options.D: The successful graduation of patients into independent apartments

explanation: Spot on! When patients stay in a hospital for too long, they can become overly dependent on staff and lose confidence in caring for themselves. We call this institutionalism. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why is clear teamwork and role assignment so vital on an evacuation mission?

options.A: Cramped spaces and high-stress environments require smooth teamwork
options.B: Patients feel anxious when roles overlap during transit
options.C: Aircraft weight limits change based on who is performing procedures
options.D: Hospital regulations fine teams that overlap their clinical duties

explanation: When space is tight and time is ticking, everyone needs to know their exact job so the team can work like a well-oiled machine without getting in each other's way. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h5)

question: Your patient has a severe head injury and declining consciousness, but your clinic has no surgeon. What is your next best step?

options.A: Wait until the morning shift arrives to decide
options.B: Keep the patient locally and repeat neurological checks hourly
options.C: Discharge the patient home with family members
options.D: Initiate emergency evacuation to a surgical center

explanation: You've got this! When local resources fall short in a life-or-death emergency, arranging a prompt medevac is the safest and most responsible action. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h2)

question: A medical ward suddenly gets lots of new patients needing extra IV cannulas and dressings. Which budget item will go up?

options.A: Capital expenditure
options.B: Overhead revenue
options.C: Fixed costs
options.D: Variable costs

explanation: Spot on! Supplies like cannulas and dressings go up and down directly with patient volume, making them classic variable costs. [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is a key characteristic of an effective nursing standard?

options.A: It should be written in complex legal language
options.B: It must change every single week
options.C: It should ignore available ward resources
options.D: It must be measurable and achievable

explanation: Effective standards must be realistic for staff to meet and clear enough to measure accurately. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h3)

question: Which type of research focuses mostly on numbers, math, and statistics?

options.A: Quantitative
options.B: Ethnographic
options.C: Qualitative
options.D: Phenomenological

explanation: Fantastic! Think 'Q for Quantity'—quantitative research deals with numbers and statistical analysis. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T2#GNS224_U1_T2_h6)

question: At what capacity should a waste bag be securely closed and removed?

options.A: As soon as the shift ends, regardless of fullness
options.B: When it is completely stuffed to the top brim
options.C: When it reaches about three-quarters full

question: Why do patients with diabetes need frequent blood sugar checks after an abortion?

options.C: Abortion procedures automatically cure diabetes
options.D: Blood sugar levels always drop to zero

question: When a nurse is assessing a teen for ICT addiction, which of these approaches should be avoided?

options.A: Scolding the teenager for wasting time on useless games

options.C: Evaluating nighttime sleep habits and bedtime routines
options.D: Asking about changes in school performance and grades

explanation: Never judge or scold! As nurses, we want to build trust so patients feel safe opening up to us without fear of being lectured. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T14#GNS312_U3_T14_h5)

question: Which sign is a strong indicator of a catheter-associated urinary tract infection?

options.C: Bright red blood in the stool
options.D: Sudden swelling of the lower legs

question: What is a major effect of malnutrition in school children?

options.C: Rapid acceleration in physical height and bone density
options.D: Increased ability to focus for long hours

explanation: That's right! Without proper nutrients, the body and brain struggle, leading to poor concentration, tiredness, and frequent sickness. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why do nurses look at reproductive health as a lifelong journey rather than just a passing phase?

options.A: Because reproductive needs change and persist from birth to old age
options.B: Because healthcare funding is tied to lifelong patient monitoring
options.C: Because reproductive organs never undergo natural degeneration
options.D: Because patients only seek care during their childbearing years

explanation: Spot on! Reproductive health matters at every single stage of life, meaning our care and guidance as nurses never truly stop. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h1)

question: When should a nurse use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: When the clinic runs out of clean disposable gloves

options.C: Before opening every single new vaccine vial
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

question: Why do nurses use standard screening tools like the Patient Health Questionnaire in clinical practice?

options.A: To quantify and measure depression symptom severity
options.B: To measure blood levels of neurotransmitters
options.C: To test physical strength and muscular endurance
options.D: To diagnose specific neurological brain disorders

explanation: Exactly! Screening tools give us a clear, structured way to score how severe a patient's depressive symptoms are so we can track their progress. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T2#GNS324_U4_T2_h4)

question: When is injectable artesunate preferred over oral malaria medications?

options.A: As a daily dietary supplement for pregnant women
options.B: When treating mild stomach ulcers caused by amoebas
options.C: In cases of severe, complicated malaria where oral intake is impossible
options.D: For routine outpatient prevention in healthy travelers

explanation: You got it! Severe malaria requires fast action through the IV or IM route because waiting on oral meds isn't safe for a very sick patient. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T5#GNS223_U3_T5_h4)

question: Where is the best spot to place a sharps container in the treatment room?

options.A: Underneath the sink in the staff breakroom
options.B: Inside a locked storage room down the hall
options.C: High up on a shelf outside patient reach
options.D: As close as possible to where procedures occur

explanation: Having the box right beside you means you never have to walk across the room carrying a used needle. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h5)

question: In conservative communities, how is family honor often tied to female family members?

options.A: Through their ability to generate personal business wealth

options.C: Through their election into local political office
options.D: Through their perceived sexual purity and chastity

question: Why is it important to evaluate the primary caregiver during a home visit?

options.A: Caregivers are legally responsible for paying the nurse's salary
options.B: Caregivers often experience burnout and physical exhaustion
options.C: Caregivers usually have the same psychiatric diagnosis
options.D: Caregivers make all clinical decisions without medical advice

explanation: Family caregivers carry immense stress supporting a mentally ill relative, making their well-being a crucial focus of home care. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h4)

question: In James Reason's famous Swiss cheese model of safety, what do the holes in the cheese represent?

options.A: The exact time a medication is due
options.B: Gaps in nursing school curriculum
options.C: The total number of patients admitted to a ward
options.D: Weaknesses in individual safety defense layers

explanation: Think of each cheese slice as a safety barrier. The holes are just the temporary cracks or flaws in those defenses. [learn more](GST319_U5_T4#GST319_U5_T4_h2)

question: A postoperative patient asks to have her temperature taken rectally. What is the correct nursing response?

options.A: Refuse to check her temperature at all during the entire hospital stay
options.B: Perform the rectal temperature quickly and gently with lots of lubrication
options.C: Ask the patient to insert the thermometer herself to avoid causing pain
options.D: Explain that rectal temperatures are contraindicated to protect the surgical repair

explanation: Any instrument placed in the rectum can damage the fresh surgical repair site and cause the surgery to fail. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h8)

question: A patient says they want to stop eating all carbs immediately to lose weight fast. As their nurse, what is your best response?

options.A: Ignore their plan and give them a rigid calorie chart
options.B: Encourage them to double their water intake instead
options.C: Help them set smaller, realistic goals for gradual change
options.D: Tell them to stop eating completely for three days

explanation: Brilliant! Slow, steady lifestyle changes stick around much longer than sudden, painful restrictions. Guide them step by step. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h3)

question: Why is a blame-free reporting culture so helpful for improving safety on hospital wards?

options.A: It speeds up the process of investigating patient complaints about pain
options.B: It allows the hospital to avoid paying for expensive safety-engineered needles
options.C: It encourages staff to report near-misses and hazards so systemic fixes can be made
options.D: It ensures that nurses never face disciplinary action for deliberate negligence

explanation: When staff feel safe speaking up without fear of being shouted at or punished, everyone can work together to fix dangerous workplace problems. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T4#GNS122_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which type of precaution requires the use of a negative pressure isolation room?

options.A: Contact precautions
options.B: Airborne precautions
options.C: Droplet precautions
options.D: Standard precautions

explanation: Negative pressure rooms prevent tiny airborne germs from drifting out into the hallway when the door is opened. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h4)

question: Why must a chest drainage system always be placed lower than the patient's chest?

options.A: To make it easier for the patient to walk around the unit
options.B: To ensure the water seal chamber bubbles continuously
options.C: To use gravity to keep fluid draining away from the pleural cavity
options.D: To prevent the suction regulator from breaking

explanation: You nailed it! Gravity is our helper here; keeping the canister low ensures fluid drains out of the chest and doesn't flow back in. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T18#GNS221_U2_T18_h4)

question: Why do state or regional health schemes often exist alongside a national scheme?

options.A: To address local health priorities and specific regional demographics
options.B: To compete directly with private international clinics
options.C: To prevent rural residents from visiting city hospitals
options.D: To collect extra taxes without government approval

explanation: Correct! State schemes let local governments customize health packages to fit the unique cultural and financial needs of their own people. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h3)

question: Under the Abuja Declaration, what percentage of their annual budget should African governments put toward health?

options.A: Five percent of private sector corporate profits

question: What is the very first priority when managing a patient who presents with acute shock?

options.A: Restoring adequate airway, breathing, and circulation
options.B: Preparing the patient for major exploratory surgery
options.C: Lowering the body temperature with cooling blankets
options.D: Administering broad-spectrum oral antibiotics immediately

question: Which drug class is commonly used to help with burning or shooting nerve pain?

options.A: Antacids
options.B: Blood thinners
options.C: Anticonvulsants
options.D: Loop diuretics

question: What is the main danger of failing to do regular reassessments in emergency care?

options.A: Doctors will forget to write discharge prescriptions
options.B: The patient will complain about hospital food quality
options.C: Subtle signs of clinical deterioration may be missed until it is too late
options.D: Insurance companies will refuse to pay the hospital bill

explanation: Regular checks help you catch failing vital signs early, giving you time to step in before things take a turn for the worse. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T2#GNS315_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is the main underlying problem in cardiogenic shock?

options.A: A massive infection spreading through the body
options.B: The heart pump fails to circulate enough blood
options.C: A severe allergic reaction to dust
options.D: Sudden blood loss from an open wound

explanation: Cardiogenic shock means the heart itself is simply too weak to pump blood forward. It's a pump failure, unlike shock from bleeding where you've lost fluid volume. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T14#GNS213_U1_T14_h5)

question: Which of these foods should a patient expect to cause extra gas and strong odor?

options.A: Plain steamed rice

options.D: White toast and butter

question: A patient has a BMI of 32.5. How is this classified?

options.D: Underweight

question: What is the main goal of performing a colposcopy in a clinic setting?

options.A: To surgically remove the entire uterus and surrounding lymph nodes

options.C: To destroy pre-cancerous lesions using extreme freezing temperatures
options.D: To magnify and closely inspect the cervix for abnormal tissue

explanation: Spot on! A colposcope is basically a special magnifying glass with a light. It helps healthcare providers get a close-up look at the surface of the cervix to check for any trouble spots. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h6)

question: What happens to your pupil when you walk from a dark room into bright sunlight?

options.A: It turns completely white and opaque

options.C: It flattens out against the cornea
options.D: It dilates to capture more light rays

question: How do HEPA filters keep a surgical patient safe?

options.D: By increasing the humidity levels inside the room

question: What is the general age range for adolescents according to the World Health Organization?

question: What is a common research duty for a bedside staff nurse?

question: How do seasonal disease trends influence how a nurse orders ward supplies?

question: Which channel is most appropriate when trying to reach healthcare policymakers?

question: Which common everyday drink should patients with anxiety and phobias cut back on because it triggers jitters and a fast heart rate?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Caffeine

options.D: Calcium

question: When an IT committee is choosing computers for an outpatient clinic, what should guide their choice?

options.A: Matching the device processing capability to daily clinical workflow needs

options.C: Selecting analog hardware to measure physical wave signals
options.D: Choosing the most expensive mainframe system for single-user desks

question: When washing hands as a food handler, how long should you scrub with soap and water?

options.B: Until they feel completely dry

question: A community health nurse is planning a schistosomiasis prevention program in a rural Nigerian village. Which action will provide the most lasting protection?

question: Which hormone is released in pulses by the hypothalamus to wake up the pituitary gland?

options.C: Luteinizing Hormone

question: What did the old FDA pregnancy Category X label mean for a medication?

options.C: Fetal risks clearly outweighed any potential therapeutic benefit
options.D: The drug was completely safe for use at any gestational age

question: Why is it smart to include family members in outpatient nutrition teaching?

question: A family caring for a young adult with a spinal cord injury insists on doing everything for them, refusing to let them try dressing themselves. What is this family showing?

question: Which of these is a key nursing task during a mass casualty incident?

question: What does the FIFO inventory method mean?

question: How do standard clinical guidelines across a health network help patients?

options.C: It allows nurses to perform major surgeries without physician supervision

question: A mother brings her 3-day-old baby to the clinic with severe jaundice and mentions storing baby clothes with traditional camphor. What likely caused this?

question: Why do nurses have to change how they normally work when responding to a field disaster?

options.A: Basic utilities and sterile spaces are usually missing

options.D: Physicians are rarely present during emergencies

explanation: Great thinking! Out in the field, you won't find normal hospital comforts like constant running water or steady electricity, so nurses have to adapt cleverly and safely. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T4#GNS315_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why is primary health care considered a philosophy rather than just a place to treat sick people?

options.C: It requires all nurses to hold a university degree in philosophy

explanation: Think of primary health care as a mindset! It's an entire value system centered on fairness, community involvement, and stopping illness before it even starts. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which position usually helps make chest pain feel better when a patient has pericarditis?

options.A: Reclining deeply with legs elevated

question: Which level of government in Nigeria typically manages primary health centers?

question: How do checklists help prevent unfair or biased observations in a study?

options.C: By removing human judgment completely from the process
options.D: By hiding the study goals from the clinical staff

question: What is a major risk of running a complete no-blame culture?

options.A: It increases the cost of buying hospital medical equipment
options.B: It completely stops communication between doctors and nurses
options.C: It fails to hold people accountable for reckless and dangerous actions

explanation: Total immunity can protect unsafe, reckless behavior. Balance is key to keeping patients safe! [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h2)

question: Which part of the chain of infection do standard precautions target the most?

question: What happens to the airways in your lungs when the sympathetic nervous system kicks in?

options.B: Bronchodilation
options.C: Bronchoconstriction
options.D: Increased mucus secretion

question: A client who just got a copper IUD a month ago complains of slightly heavier periods and mild cramps. What is your best response as her nurse?

options.D: Reassure her that this is normal at first and discuss pain relief

question: What is a major benefit of keeping synovial fluid moving inside a joint?

options.A: It cools down the body when a fever is present.

options.C: It permanently locks the joint in a straight position.

question: An audit shows nurses forget pain scores because the chart has no space for them. What is the best fix?

options.A: Suspending every nurse working on the ward without pay
options.B: Banning the use of all written documents on the hospital ward
options.C: Telling patients they must diagnose their own pain levels

question: How does strong teamwork across hospital departments act as a safety net for patients?

options.C: It removes all documentation requirements from the nursing shift
options.D: It ensures that patients never need to take any medications

question: What does a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) primarily aim to discover?

options.C: Which specific nurse made the final active mistake
options.D: Whether the doctor wrote the medication order correctly

question: A nurse wants to know if a new wound dressing heals ulcers faster. What is her very first step?

question: Which muscle group is primarily activated by the femoral nerve?

question: How does an occupational therapist mostly differ from a physiotherapist?

question: Which parts of the body usually show signs of vitamin or nutrient shortages first?

question: What is the main goal of having both the sympathetic and parasympathetic systems working together?

options.A: Maintaining a stable internal body balance

question: Why must researchers follow a standardized procedure during data collection?

question: Why are women in active labour usually advised not to eat heavy solid foods?

question: What is the main reason we use the coefficient of variation in research?

question: Why are pregnant women and young children grouped together as a special population?

question: Which part of the teenage brain is still maturing and plays a big role in impulse control and risk-taking?

question: Standard X-rays are most helpful for looking at which part of the body?

question: Why might ethical rules stop a nurse researcher from using an experimental design for certain topics?

question: What happens directly to patients when public health funding is poorly managed?

question: What is the safest way to carry a full medical waste bag?

question: What does a Non-Stress Test (NST) actually check for?

question: What is the primary purpose of an Institutional Review Board (IRB) in research?

question: What is a run chart mainly used for on a hospital ward?

question: What is the main job of NEMA when a big disaster hits?

question: Why is knowing research classifications important for evidence-based nursing?

options.C: To pump blood throughout the body systems
options.D: To protect and support internal organs

explanation: Body cavities act as safe, enclosed spaces that cushion internal organs against physical trauma. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why do nurses closely monitor blood potassium levels in patients taking loop diuretics?

options.A: Loop diuretics cause the body to lose potassium in the urine
options.B: Potassium prevents the patient from developing a dry cough
options.C: Potassium levels determine the correct dose of furosemide
options.D: High potassium levels stop the diuretic from working completely

explanation: Spot on! Loop diuretics flush out water, but they drag important potassium along with it. Keeping an eye on labs helps us prevent dangerous low potassium (hypokalemia). [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h4)

question: A nurse notices pressure sores are common in the elderly ward and tries a new turning schedule. What is this an example of?

options.A: An illegal medical experiment on vulnerable human subjects
options.B: A quality improvement project based on clinical observation
options.C: A violation of hospital administrative policy
options.D: A financial investment in medical equipment manufacturing

explanation: Spot on! Noticing a ward problem and trying a practical nursing fix to make things better is a classic quality improvement project. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T6#GNS217_U2_T6_h5)

question: What do we call a strange, unexpected drug reaction that happens because of a patient's unique genetics?

options.A: Therapeutic side effect
options.B: Anaphylactic shock
options.C: Idiosyncratic reaction
options.D: Cumulative toxicity

explanation: Idiosyncratic means it's a rare, one-of-a-kind reaction that catches everyone by surprise based on body chemistry. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T2#GNS125_U1_T2_h6)

question: A nurse is preparing to send a patient home for the weekend. What is the most important action regarding medications?

options.A: Ensuring the correct medication supply is packaged with clear instructions for the family
options.B: Telling the patient to stop all medications for the weekend break
options.C: Asking the family to buy medications from an unregistered market
options.D: Hiding the medication supply in the suitcase without telling anyone

explanation: Clear labels and proper medication supplies prevent missed doses and keep the patient safe and stable all weekend long. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h6)

question: Which lab test is checked regularly for a patient on an unfractionated heparin drip?

options.A: Complete blood cell count only
options.B: Bleeding time and platelet function
options.C: Prothrombin time and INR
options.D: Activated partial thromboplastin time

explanation: We use the aPTT test to make sure our patient is getting just the right amount of heparin—not too little, not too much. Perfect clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h3)

question: How does nursing care in a half-way house differ from an acute hospital ward?

options.A: It focuses on rehabilitation, education, and community reintegration
options.B: It requires nurses to diagnose patients without a doctor present
options.C: It forbids nurses from talking to patients about their feelings
options.D: It relies entirely on physical restraints and locked isolation cells

explanation: Correct! Instead of dealing with emergency crises, residential nursing is all about teaching coping skills, guiding rehabilitation, and helping patients reconnect with society. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h6)

question: Why is it important for clinical nurses to understand basic legal frameworks regarding harmful practices?

options.A: To recognize mandatory reporting duties and protect vulnerable patients
options.B: To arrest individuals who bring injured patients to the hospital
options.C: To write new bills for the national legislative assembly
options.D: To act as defense attorneys during court trials for offenders

explanation: Nurses must know when the law requires reporting child abuse or imminent danger to child protection authorities. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h3)

question: Which main nerve links the gastrointestinal tract directly to the brain?

options.A: The phrenic nerve
options.B: The trigeminal nerve
options.C: The vagus nerve
options.D: The sciatic nerve

explanation: Spot on! The vagus nerve is the primary communication highway connecting your gut and your brain. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h1)

question: In Vroom's Expectancy Theory, what does the term 'valence' mean?

options.A: The belief that effort leads to good performance
options.B: The physical effort required for a clinical task
options.C: The guarantee that a reward will be delivered
options.D: The value an individual places on a specific reward

explanation: Valence is simply how much you actually want or care about the reward being offered. If management offers a prize you don't care about, your valence is low! [learn more](GST321_U3_T6#GST321_U3_T6_h3)

question: A ward introduces hourly rounds to stop patient falls. Tracking whether the nurses actually completed those hourly rounds is an example of what?

options.A: Process measure
options.B: Baseline measure
options.C: Balancing measure
options.D: Outcome measure

explanation: Spot on! A process measure simply checks whether the specific steps or tasks in our care plan are actually being carried out day-to-day. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why do established rectovaginal fistulas rarely heal on their own?

options.A: The tract becomes lined with epithelium
options.B: Bowel movements constantly stretch the perineum
options.C: Vaginal acidity dissolves new tissue growth
options.D: Continuous high blood pressure prevents clotting

explanation: Once epithelial tissue lines the abnormal passage, the body treats the tract as a normal surface, preventing natural closure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h2)

question: Which of these should normally NOT slip through the kidney's filter into your urine?

options.A: Sodium mineral ions
options.B: Filtered water molecules
options.C: Large plasma proteins
options.D: Dissolved glucose molecules

explanation: Correct! A healthy kidney filter has tiny pores that keep big things like proteins and blood cells safely inside your bloodstream. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T6#GNS121_U2_T6_h2)
